rule_level_problems.problem: The priority rule's evidence (Cardiac arrest, Absent pulse) is not checked for anywhere in this file, so it satisfies the house test only if one of those concepts is a registered warning sign or common symptom. If neither is, the rule has no trigger the system records and the test's priority-evidence constraint fails. The same two findings are the due_to of the check_for task and the and-gate of both probable rules, so everything on the page hangs on them being recordable.

The page's discriminating finding, the heart rhythm (VF / pVT / asystole / PEA), appears nowhere. Every flowchart branch and the 'decide when to stop CPR' box turn on it, and SNOMED has exact concepts for all four. The file encodes only the two 'look for cause' diagnoses and the entry trigger, so the flowchart is lost.

Expressible thresholds dropped: glucose < 3 mmol/L (< 4 if diabetic) and temperature ≤ 35 °C are routine vitals with units in the language, and the page uses them twice (reversible causes; decide when to stop). Possible Hypoglycemia and possible Hypothermia rules gated on cardiac arrest would carry them and hand off to pages 19 and 18.

Adding them needs a consuming rule (a possible diagnosis or priority) to pass the 'checked for but never used' test, which is probably why they were omitted; the omission should at least be recorded as a known gap.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Thirst due to water deprivation' (finding) is a child of 'Thirst finding' (finding) and asserts a cause the page does not; the page says only 'thirst'. The parent concept exists and is the closer match.

Diarrhoea/vomiting are listed by the page alongside dehydration as reasons for the fluid bolus; they are common symptoms so no check item is needed, but no rule on this page consumes them. Defensible under the no-manage-tasks rule; noted so the gap is deliberate.

summary: The two 'X likely' conclusions the page states (tension pneumothorax; dehydration from footnote 2) and the Emergency no-pulse trigger are encoded correctly, with verified concepts and the page's any-of logic. The main gaps are that the heart rhythm, the page's discriminating finding, is absent from the file entirely, and that the glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) and temperature ≤ 35 °C thresholds, which the language can express as routine vitals, are not encoded even as possible Hypoglycemia / Hypothermia hand-offs to pages 19 and 18. Trauma, snake bite and overdose/poisoning are listed as causes to look for but are not checked, and the priority rule depends on Cardiac arrest / Absent pulse being recordable as a warning sign, which this file does not itself guarantee.
